subject: forestSpirit
reasoning:
I'm planning out a single TypeScript module to construct a stylized low-poly forest spirit, mapping out the builder API for joints, chains, and roles before writing the actual generation code.

I'm sketching the design: a roughly 2.2m tall humanoid figure with branch-like antler horns, a leafy crown, bark-textured torso with mossy paint, glowing eyes, flowing leaf-cloak cards, and root-like feet, all within the part/triangle/joint budget limits, using a lathe-based profile for the tapered bark torso.

Now I'm planning the joint hierarchy -- hips as the root, chest parented to it, then a neck chain up to the head -- and the head geometry as a stylized sphere with small glowing eye spheres and antler chains branching off.

Antlers get built as swept branches tapering from thick base to thin tips, bone-anchored to the head joint, while arms follow a similar pattern: shoulder, elbow, wrist joints connected by capsule segments bound to those bones.

Defining the leg chains next, mirroring the arm setup with hip, knee, and ankle joints along a similar polyline structure.

I'll attach the torso lathe to the chest joint instead, using a tall rounded profile curve that tapers at the top and flares slightly at the hips.

Switching to loft for the body makes more sense since it allows bone weighting toward joints like hips and chest, giving smoother skin deformation than the lathe approach. For coloring, I'm thinking of layering bark grain textures with mossy mottling to give the trunk-like body a natural, weathered look.

For the leaf cards, I'd use a leaf SVG texture mapped onto ring-generated frames around the crown — placing cards in a circular arrangement around the head joint, tilted and spread for a natural canopy effect.

For hanging cloak leaves, I'm thinking a similar ring around the chest or shoulders, but angled downward with flow pointing down and leaned closer to the body surface, so they drape like foliage rather than sticking straight out.

For the leaf texture itself, I'm sketching an SVG with a tapered leaf outline filled green and a darker vein stroke down the middle, which will rasterize fine when the showcase renders it. For the eyes I'll just use a bright pale cyan color since there's no true emissive support. Now I'm starting to think through the antler geometry as a branching sweep path from the head outward.

Setting up the skeleton hierarchy now: hips as root with spine role, chest and neck as parents up the chain, and head attached to neck. I'm also defining a spine chain joining the hips and chest joints for proper bending.

So I need to create the root joint explicitly first via b.joint for "hips", since chains can't start as root. Then the spine chain needs a new name instead of reusing "hips" to avoid conflicts, so I'll rename the chain's joints accordingly and set its parent to the existing hips joint.

Instead I'll just build the full skeleton joint-by-joint: hips (root, spine), chest, neck, head — each parented to the previous with appropriate roles and positions. For the arms, I'll use a chain starting at the shoulder parented to chest, with joints named shoulderL/elbowL/handL following the polyline path, then sweep a tapered tube along that chain for the arm geometry.

For hands I'm thinking of a small scaled sphere for the palm plus a few thin rod "fingers" extending from the hand joint position, binding them to the handL bone so they follow the arm rig correctly.

Now I'm building a mirrored limb helper so left/right sides reuse the same code with a sign flip, setting up the leg chains (hip, knee, ankle) parented to hips, and placing foot spheres scaled flat so their bottoms sit just above the floor within tolerance.

For the torso I'm lofting through hip, waist, chest, shoulder, and neck stations with bark coloring, skinned to the hips/chest/neck bones, and deciding to skip a cloak membrane for reliability while considering a mossy mantle or leaf cape around the shoulders, then starting on the antler sweep from the head joint.

Now I'm defining the antler geometry as mirrored sweep paths with tapering radii, adding a branch sweep, and placing small leaf-bud spheres at the tips bound to the head bone, then starting on the bark-and-moss colored head sphere.

For the head I'm skipping an actual carved mask and just adding glowing eye spheres, then setting up a ring of crown leaves around the head using tilt and lean parameters so they angle upward and outward from the surface.

Now I'm working through a skirt of leaves ringed around the hips, tilted downward and outward using negative tilt and flow parameters so they hang like a skirt, and starting to plan a partial arc ring at the chest for a shoulder cape, deciding on angle ranges so it wraps around the back.

I'm checking the radii against actual torso widths at each joint height to make sure the skirt and cape rings sit outside the body mesh rather than clipping into it, adjusting the chest radius upward since the torso is wider there than my initial estimate.

Now I'm sketching mushroom shapes using a lathe profile—small polygon points defining a stem and cap cross-section—to add as decorative details on the shoulders and hips, anchored to the bone joints. I'm also setting up paint textures combining grainy bark colors and mottled moss greens for the overall skin material.

For the body paint, I decide a hard switch between moss and bark based on the surface normal's vertical component rather than trying to blend two paints together. I'm picking a soft glowing teal for the eyes and planning minimal facial details—just eyes and maybe a small nose ridge—before moving on to building the arm chain starting from the chest joint.

Now I'm working out hand and finger geometry, placing small spheres and rods at computed joint positions for the hands and fingers, figuring out torso and leg proportions so the whole figure comes out around 2.2 meters tall, and starting to set up the necessary imports for the geometry and painting utilities.

Writing module imports and leaf SVG...

Adding neck and head joints...

Still working out the sweep radius typing...

Now I'm defining the hand geometry as a scaled sphere attached to the arm bone, then setting up finger dimensions as small rod segments with varying length, taper, and thickness ratios.

For legs, I'm building a joint chain from hip to knee to ankle with decreasing tube radius, and attaching sphere-based feet at the ankle, scaling them to sit flush with the ground.

Then I'm defining the torso using a loft through five stations from hips up through chest to neck, tapering widths and heights, bound to the hips/chest/neck joint chain. The neck tapers to meet the head sphere positioned on top, closing out the upper body shape.

I'm sketching facial features now: a brow box, a cone-shaped nose aimed forward-down, and eyes built from small glowing spheres layered over darker socket spheres flattened along the z-axis for depth.

Now I'm turning to the antlers, sweeping a curved branching shape outward and upward from the head with tapering radii, choosing a pale bone-like color for a forest spirit look rather than plain bark, and starting a secondary branch forking off the main antler path.

For the antler buds and crown, I'm placing small sphere nodes at the branch tips for leaf attachment points, then setting up a ring of leaf cards around the head using the ring helper to position items at an angle and distance from center, checking whether the radius is large enough to clear the head sphere given the tilt.

I'm also building a hanging skirt of leaves around the hips using a similar ring-based approach, with downward tilt and varied bend so the leaves drape outward and down from the body.

Then I'm adding a back cape made of leaves arranged in a partial ring around the chest, spanning roughly the back arc from 120 to 240 degrees so they hang down from mid-chest level with a steep lean.

Now I'm starting to sketch out a mushroom cap profile using a lathe shape, defining the curve points for its radius and height.

Writing lathe points...

I'm positioning two small mushrooms on the body surface — one near the torso tilted outward along a diagonal axis so it sprouts sideways naturally, and another near the hip area, making sure their placement roughly matches the body's ellipse contour so they look like they're growing from the surface.

I'm also adding mossy sphere clumps on the shoulders using a flattened scale, checking my paint functions (moss/bark blend based on normal direction, mottle and grain texture helpers) and geometry constructors (sphere segments, cone dimensions) to make sure everything is typed correctly before I return the finished root mesh.
